commitments.text: The Project will continue to operate as a daily peaking plant within current license requirements.

BC Hydro will prepare an Environmental Management Plan (EMP) prior to commencement of the construction phase to provide guidance on actions and activities that will be implemented during construction to mitigate potential adverse impacts. The EMP will be submitted to the appropriate environmental agency for acceptance before work commences and will include the following component plans: Sediment and Erosion Control Plan; Oil Spill Prevention and Emergency Response Plan; Water Quality Monitoring Plan; Construction Waste Management Plan; Cementitious Materials Control Plan; Air Quality and Dust Control Plan; Traffic Safety Management Plan; Health and Safety Plan; Landscape Design and Site Restoration Plan; Terrestrial Habitat Mitigation Plan; Archaeological Impact Management Plan; Fish and Fish Habitat Mitigation and Compensation Plan.

BC Hydro will review and update, where applicable, general Environmental Management Procedures, as well as a site-specific Oil Spill Prevention and Emergency Response Plan, that currently comprise the existing Operational Environmental Management documentation for the Revelstoke Dam to reflect potential changes as a result of the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project.

BC Hydro will prepare a Decommissioning Environmental Management Plan prior to future decommissioning activities and in accordance with the regulatory regime and environmental sensitivities at that time. The Decommissioning EMP will include guidance on actions and activities to be implemented during decommissioning of the power facility to decrease potential for environmental effects.

BC Hydro will develop an Environmental Monitoring Plan to the satisfaction of DFO, which will identify the type and frequency of observations and data collection, methodologies to be employed, and protocols to be followed.

BC Hydro will retain a qualified environmental monitor to inspect, evaluate and report on the performance of construction activities, and the effectiveness of environmental control strategies and mitigation measures, with respect to regulatory permits, approvals, and authorizations, environmental legislation, and BMPs. The monitor will be on site whenever there is elevated potential risk to the environment and will report directly to the Construction Manager.

BC Hydro will develop and implement a bank erosion protection monitoring and mitigation program to identify and address current and future shoreline erosion concerns downstream of Revelstoke Dam (Revelstoke Golf Course, and mid Columbia River between Trans Canada Highway bridge and Begbie Creek).

BC Hydro will remove the concrete plug materials from the draft tube in the dry by dewatering the work area and will clean up and dispose of any residual materials in accordance with accepted practices.
If deemed necessary by BC MOE, BC Hydro will restrict angling activities of non-local workforce to mitigate potential increased angling pressure and harvest effects on sport fish populations.

BC Hydro will review and adapt Columbia River WUP monitoring programs to incorporate the evaluation of potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam on fish and aquatic habitat, with emphasis on white sturgeon.

BC Hydro will commit to entering into discussions with Regulatory Agencies and First Nations to develop possible mitigation and compensation options in the event that Revelstoke Unit 5 Project specific or WUP related monitoring programs indicate a negative effect of the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project on water quality, fish, or valuable ecosystem components (VECs).

BC Hydro will develop a mitigation or compensation plan for entrainment at Revelstoke Dam (including Unit 5 incremental impacts) if deemed required through BC Hydro's Fish Entrainment Strategy and Risk Assessment.

BC Hydro will re-establish vegetation following completion of the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project construction phase. Establishment of native plant species will be accomplished through seeding with a succession mix matched to the site characteristics.
BC Hydro will conduct follow-up monitoring of revegetation efforts on the construction site to ensure that noxious weeds do not become prevalent and that full restoration of the site is achieved.

BC Hydro will review and adapt the Columbia River WUP revegetation physical works program for the mid-Columbia River and Arrow Lakes to incorporate the potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam.
BC Hydro will, when possible, schedule vegetation clearing for the temporary materials storage, parking areas and spoil disposal sites outside of the breeding bird season (01 April to 31 July).
BC Hydro will, when possible, restrict construction machinery to a flagged clearing area.
BC Hydro will revegetate disturbed sites as soon as possible after completion of construction.
BC Hydro will develop and implement a detailed list of replacement habitat features and specifications to mitigate impacts on wildlife habitat at the Project site.
BC Hydro will conduct surveys prior to construction to confirm that no eagle or osprey nests are located within 500 m of the construction site.

BC Hydro will discourage nesting of Barn Swallow in areas of scheduled construction activities (e.g., netting). If active nests are found within the Unit 5 bulkhead area, construction activities that require removal of the nest would not occur during the time when the nest is occupied by a bird or egg. If nesting birds appear to be disturbed by construction noises, then BC Hydro would consult with CWS regarding appropriate construction timing to minimize nest disturbance.
BC Hydro will, when possible, restrict use of Westside Road during the night when ungulates and carnivores are active and vehicle-wildlife collisions are more likely to occur.

BC Hydro will conduct surveys prior to construction to determine the location of suitable amphibian and reptile ponds and upland habitat in relation to roads that would be used by construction traffic.
BC Hydro will monitor wildlife mortalities on Westside Road and the dam access road throughout the construction phase.
BC Hydro will review and adapt the draft Columbia River WUP wildlife habitat physical works program to incorporate the potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam.
BC Hydro will conduct an archaeological impact assessment prior to any bank stabilization project that involves the disturbance of intact terrace sediments.
BC Hydro will review and adapt the Columbia River WUP archaeological site protection program for Arrow Lakes Reservoir to incorporate the potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam.
BC Hydro will investigate options to provide housing for the in-migrating Unit 5 work force.

BC Hydro will employ qualified local workers if available and where appropriate to carry out Project activities. BC Hydro's contractors will follow the CHC Agreement, which includes provisions for local hiring preferences.
30. BC Hydro will provide a Project Liaison person in the City of Revelstoke to address project-related inquiries

31. BC Hydro will monitor the condition of Westside Road, including the Jordan River Bridge, and will commit to an equitable proportion of the maintenance costs above what would normally be required over the construction period for specific damage to the road caused by the Project.
32. BC Hydro will inform its contractors to adhere to posted construction speed limits
33. BC Hydro will, when possible, maintain access to the Revelstoke Dam Visitor Centre during construction

34. BC Hydro will inform helicopter companies (i.e. Canadian Mountain Helicopters, Sekirk Mountain Helicopters) well in advance about any project-related road closures or other construction-related activities that could affect their flight paths
35. BC Hydro will adhere to City of Revelstoke noise bylaw, and encourage car pooling of the construction workforce
36. BC Hydro will review public information signage for the mid Columbia River Drawdown Zone to incorporate any changes necessary as a result of the installation of the fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam

37. BC Hydro will review the Public Safety Management Plan for the Revelstoke and Arrow Lakes Reservoirs to incorporate any changes necessary to reflect the installation of the fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam
38. BC Hydro will review and adapt the Columbia River WUP boat access improvement plan to incorporate the potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam

39. BC Hydro will review navigational buoy/channel marker installation and public information signage for the mid Columbia River to incorporate any changes necessary as a result of the installation of the fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam

40. BC Hydro will require all contractors working on site to adhere to Worker Compensation Board regulations, and adhere to all applicable standards and codes, including those of the Canadian Standards Association.

41. All equipment used on the project site will be fitted with standard emission control devices appropriate to the equipment and in compliance with federal, provincial and municipal regulations and standards

42. Dust from on-site construction activities will be controlled in compliance with the Worker's Compensation Board Industrial Health and Safety Regulations. Chemical dust suppressants such as calcium lignosulphate, sodium lignosulphate or magnesium chloride will not be employed
43. BC Hydro will implement routine safety procedures outlined in its Public Safety Management Plan for the Revelstoke Facility during construction of the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project
44. First aid attendants will be stationed at the work site and emergency evacuation vehicles will be stationed within close proximity
45. The power house and work yard will have security fencing around the perimeters

46. During the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project, BC Hydro will continue to comply with its Sewage Treatment Maintenance Standard, in accordance with provincial statutory regulations governing sewage treatment systems
47. All structures and facilities constructed for the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project will be designed to meet the requirements of the National Building Code of Canada
48. Detailed engineering drawings for the Project will be prepared and sealed by Registered Professional Engineers, licensed and authorized to practice in British Columbia
49. During construction, all works will be inspected to confirm compliance with engineering specifications

50. BC Hydro will employ due diligence and adhere to applicable legislation such as the Wildfire Act and Regulation and Forest and Range Practices Act to minimize potential risk of wildfire hazards during construction of the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project
51. BC Hydro will continue to implement the existing Emergency Response Plan for the Revelstoke Facility during any catastrophic event occurring at the dam

52. All work at the generation site will continue to be screened for environmental risk and an environmental management plan prepared if required. Contractors conducting work with environmental risk will be given a documented orientation to the environmental management plan and follow the plan

53. Generation staff will continue to be provided with environmental training including Oil Spill Prevention and Response, Transportation of Dangerous Goods, Hazardous Waste Management, Working in and Around Water and a variety of other training related to the Environmental Management System
54. BC Hydro will continue to implement existing Environmental BMPs and procedures in place for the Revelstoke Dam
55. Fuelling and work areas where spills have the potential to occur will incorporate berms or other mitigation measures to minimize the potential for fuel releases into the environment
56. Hazardous materials will be stored off site and only small amounts will be brought to site as required
57. Equipment storage areas will be flood proof and located away areas that could be potentially flooded.
58. First Nations employment training program has been implemented in advance of project construction
59. BC Hydro will provide $30,000 to each First Nation to support traditional use study programs
60. First Nations hiring provisions of the Columbia Hydro Constructors agreement will continue to be applicable.
61. Traffic safety management plan will mitigate wildlife mortalities and potential impacts on subsistence harvesting. (Refer to 2 above)

62. BC Hydro will commit to entering into discussions with First Nations to develop possible mitigation and compensation options in the event that monitoring indicates a negative effect of the project on water quality (Refer to 11 above)

63. BC Hydro will review and adapt the Columbia River WUP revegetation physical works program for the mid-Columbia River and Arrow Lakes to incorporate the potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam in order to mitigate potential impacts on subsistence harvesting. (Refer to 15 above)

64. BC Hydro will, when possible, schedule vegetation clearing for the temporary materials storage, parking areas and spoil disposal sites outside of the breeding bird season (1 April to 31 July) in order to mitigate potential impacts on subsistence harvesting. (Refer to 16 above)

65. BC Hydro will review and adapt the Columbia River WUP wildlife habitat physical works program to incorporate the potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam in order to mitigate potential impacts on subsistence harvesting. (Refer to 25 above)
66. BC Hydro will conduct an archaeological impact assessment prior to any bank stabilization project that involves the disturbance of intact terrace sediments (Refer to 26 above)

67. BC Hydro will review and adapt the Columbia River WUP archaeological site protection program for Arrow Lakes Reservoir to incorporate the potential effects of a fifth unit at Revelstoke Dam (Refer to 27 above)
68. The archaeology site survey and inventory proposed by the Columbia WUP Consultative Committee be advanced to the year 2007 for the area of influence by the Revelstoke Unit 5 Project

69. Continue First Nations consultations per negotiated capacity funding agreements continue to negotiate agreement on capacity funding where not in place and negotiate other agreements on outstanding project-related issues.
